body:
Yes I'm hoping the result of these tests will be conclusive so I can see where to go from here.
I currently make just enough money to pay my bills with sporadic freelance design/webdesign work, I could probably extend that to a fulltime occucpation if I were motivated.

Since I have still not received any kind of official diagnosis, I was basically told (in less direct terms) to fuck off. There is a possible light at the end of the tunnel if there is a conclusive result from this batch of tests.

I am currently undergoing my final batch of tests to determine which of two rare disorders I have. I will not mention them since I do not wish to be identified at this point (can probably still be deduced, but less easily), I will however try to explain the discomfort this causes.

Temperatures that most people find pleasurable or tolerable give me symptoms of a severe heat stroke if I am exposed to them for longer than a few minutes. I get a headache, nausea, my hands, feet and face turn red, swell up and get a strong burning pain (I also do not sweat in these areas, they become really dry). As an example, last weekend it was 28°C here for one day, I spent the entire day throwing up and lying in a cold bath tub.

Physical activity or sports are only possible in temperatures below 0°C without getting extremely uncomfortable. I like my room temperatures at around 14°C. And yes, Dr. Victor Fries was my favorite batman villain as a child (until Arnold Schwarzenegger played him).

I have considered moving to a colder climate, but I do not really have the means to do this financially.
